transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I guess I’m here because most days I wake up already feeling low, like there’s this gray weight on me. Even when I’m at work with the crew or around my kids, I can’t really shake it. I’m there, but it feels like I’m just going through the motions.
How long have you been feeling this low most days?

About three years now… a little over that. I’d say around three years and three months. It started when our groundskeeping contract changed and the schedule got longer. Since then it’s felt like the long days just kind of took over my life.
During those three years, have there been any stretches longer than two months when you did not feel low?

No, not really. It’s been pretty steady for about three years and three months, since that contract changed and the longer schedule started. I don’t think I’ve had a stretch longer than a couple months where it actually lifted.
Do you feel your low mood is mainly a reaction to the longer work schedule that started when the contract changed?
Yeah, I think it’s tied to that. It’s been going on about three years and three months, since the contract changed and the longer days kind of took over my life.
During this time, have you ever had a period when the depression became much worse than your usual baseline for at least two weeks?
I’m not really sure. It’s been low most of the time, so it’s hard for me to separate out a clear two-week stretch where it was much worse than the rest. I haven’t really tracked it like that.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I’m not sure. I mean, I still do some things, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether I enjoy them less or not. It’s hard to say.
If your work schedule had eased up, do you think the low mood would have gone away?

I don’t know that it would’ve just gone away. The schedule made things harder, yeah, but most days I wake up already feeling this heavy, gray kind of weight on me. Even when I’m with the crew or around my kids, I still feel low and kind of hollow, like I’m just getting through the day.
Do you feel anxious or worried most days?
I’m not really sure. I worry about things here and there, like anyone, but I haven’t paid attention to whether it’s most days or not. It’s hard for me to separate that from just feeling worn down.
During these past three years, have you had any period of at least two weeks when your depression was clearly worse than your usual baseline?
I’m not sure. It’s been low for so long that I don’t really know how to separate out a clear two-week stretch as worse than the rest. There are harder days, but I haven’t tracked it that way.
Have you had trouble sleeping?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I know I’m tired a lot, but I haven’t paid close attention to whether I’m actually sleeping badly or just waking up feeling worn out.
During the past three years, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you lost interest or pleasure in almost everything?
I’m not sure. I mean, I’ve definitely had times where I didn’t enjoy much, but I can’t say for sure it was almost everything for two weeks straight. It all kind of blends together for me.
On most days, do you feel nervous or on edge?
I don’t really know. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed being nervous most days. Maybe tense sometimes, but I’m not sure I’d call it on edge.
On most days during these past three years, have you felt hopeless?

Yeah. Most days it feels like this is just how my life is now. Like no matter how hard I work or try to get back to things I used to care about, like the garden or music nights, it doesn’t really seem like anything’s going to turn around.
On most days during these past three years, have you had low energy?

Yeah. Most days I feel worn out pretty early. By midmorning, it can feel like I’ve already done a full day’s work, even when I haven’t. Even if I sleep in on a Sunday, I still drag through basic stuff—loading tools, looking over job plans, making dinner. It just feels like I don’t have much in the tank.
On most days during these past three years, have you felt bad about yourself?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean, I don’t feel great about myself a lot of the time, but I don’t know if I’d say I’ve noticed it in that exact way most days.
On most days during these past three years, has your appetite been poor or have you eaten much more than usual?
I haven’t really tracked that. I don’t think my appetite’s been the main thing, or not in a way I can clearly say it’s been most days. Some days I eat less, some days normal, but I’m not sure.
On most days during these past three years, have you had trouble concentrating or making decisions?

Yeah, I have. I miss details when I’m planning jobs, and I get behind on the crew paperwork because I just can’t keep my head on it. Even deciding what needs to be done next can take me too long.

And outside of work, I’ve been avoiding the community garden and the music gatherings I used to help organize. People have had to step in for things they used to count on me for.
On most days during these past three years, have you had low self-esteem?
I’m not sure. I don’t think of it exactly as “low self-esteem.” I know I’ve felt worn down and not like myself, but whether that’s most days or what to call it… I don’t really know.
During these past three years, was there ever a two-week period when you felt down nearly all day, every day?

Yeah. Honestly, it’s felt like that for a long time. Most days I wake up already feeling like there’s this gray weight on me, and it stays there. Even when I’m working with the crew or I’m around my kids, I still feel low and kind of hollow, like I’m just going through the motions.
During these past three years, was there ever a two-week period when you lost interest or pleasure in nearly all activities?

I don’t know if I’d say “nearly all activities.” I’ve definitely pulled back from things, but whether there was a full two weeks where I lost interest in almost everything… I’m not sure. I can’t really pin that down.
